post.summary: Resolve a ticker, name or address to tokens
post.description:
Resolves a ticker, name, prefix or `0x` address to candidate ERC-20 tokens on Arc.

- **Cost:** 0.005 USDC per call over x402: the first call gets a 402 with payment requirements in the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header (base64 JSON); sign them and retry with a `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header carrying the payment payload.
- **Key inputs:** `query` (required), `limit` (1-25, default 10).
- **Returns:** each match with its verification status, safety verdicts and USDC/hub pools, most relevant first.
- **Next:** pass the chosen result's `address` as `sell` or `buy` to POST /trade/v1/quote.

PAYMENT-RESPONSE.description: Settlement receipt for this call's payment (base64 JSON); see the SettleResponse schema for the decoded shape.

details.message: Invalid input: expected string, received undefined

500.description: internal (arcgate's own handler) or an x402 middleware internal error - neither settles payment.

post.summary: Quote a swap between two different assets
post.description:
Prices a swap between `sell` and `buy` across the indexed venues and stores it under a `quoteId`.

- **Cost:** 0.01 USDC per call over x402: the first call gets a 402 with payment requirements in the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header (base64 JSON); sign them and retry with a `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header carrying the payment payload.
- **`sell` / `buy`:** two different assets (native and ERC-20 USDC count as the same asset; either side may be USDC). Resolve a ticker with POST /trade/v1/search first.
- **Response shape:** when one side is USDC, `best.type` is `direct`/`two_hop`/`split` and `best.legs` lists one leg per path actually used; `routes[]` lists every discovery candidate. When neither side is USDC, or when a USDC-side allocation can't be expressed as legs, `best.type` is `graph`, `best.legs` is empty, and the execution plan is in `best.graph`. Both shapes support `side: exactIn` and `exactOut`, and both execute the same way through POST /trade/v1/swap.
- **`amount`:** a human-readable decimal string in the token's own units, e.g. "1.5" for 1.5 USDC, not base units. It is the `sell` amount for `side: exactIn` and the `buy` amount for `side: exactOut`.
- **Optional:** `side` (exactIn/exactOut), `slippageBps`, split and hop limits, `venues`/`excludeVenues` (ids from GET /trade/v1/venues), `taker`, `ttlSec`.
- **Executability:** POST /trade/v1/swap executes every quote through ArcgateRouter. `best.executable` is `false`, with warning `graph_execution_unavailable`, when no ArcgateRouter is configured (or, for an Aerodrome edge, no Aerodrome router), or when the operator has disabled a selected path's venue - even with both routers configured. In that last case, POST /trade/v1/swap may still fall back to an executable candidate the quote already priced instead of failing outright.
- **Readiness:** name the wallet that will trade in `taker` and the answer carries `readiness`, read at the quote's block: whether that wallet holds the input (`balance`), which approval or Permit2 signature POST /trade/v1/swap will need (`approval` for the default permit2, `approve` for `approval: "approve"`), enough native USDC for gas (`gas`), and whether this call's x402 payer can pay the swap fee (`fees`). `totalCostUsdc` is the swap fee plus gas: what finishing costs. When `ready` is false, `next` is `stop`. Without `taker` there is no `readiness`.
- **Lifetime:** the `quoteId` is good for `ttlSec` seconds (default and max 120).
- **Next:** POST /trade/v1/swap with the returned `quoteId`.

200.description: Quote, including routes, safety and the stored quoteId.

safety.note: Both endpoints are pinned assets; graph delivery was measured at the quote block.

PAYMENT-RESPONSE.description: Settlement receipt for this call's payment (base64 JSON); see the SettleResponse schema for the decoded shape.

400.description: invalid_request / ticker_not_allowed / invalid_amount / unsupported_pair / unknown_venue / unknown_source / taker_required

error.message: sell must be a 0x token address, not a ticker or name
error.hint: Resolve the ticker with POST /trade/v1/search and quote the address you pick.

post.summary: Turn a stored quote into unsigned swap transactions
post.description:
Turns a stored quote into unsigned transactions for the taker to sign and send. arcgate never signs, broadcasts or holds funds.

- **Cost:** 0.01 USDC under $1,000; 0.05 USDC from $1,000 to $10,000; above that 0.05 USDC plus 0.5 bps of the amount over $10,000, capped at 5 USDC, size-tiered by the quote's USD notional (the USDC side for a USDC pair, or a token-to-token quote's USD valuation; a quote with no valuation prices at tier 1), over x402 (402 with `PAYMENT-REQUIRED`, retry with `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`). Charged once per quote: POST /trade/v1/swap/tx, the Permit2 second round below, is free.
- **Key inputs:** `quoteId` (from POST /trade/v1/quote), `taker`; optional `recipient` (defaults to `taker`), `deadlineSec`, `approval`. Never `permit` - that belongs to POST /trade/v1/swap/tx; sending one here is 400 `invalid_request` (the strict schema rejects the unknown key).
- **Every quote executes through ArcgateRouter:** it is always the Permit2 `spender` and the ERC-20 `approve` spender below. When every source pool of the route being executed trades native USDC, the swap is funded by `value` instead - no approval transaction and no signature at all.
- **Permit2 (default, one or two calls):**
  - Returns `transactions` - an unlimited ERC-20 `approve(Permit2, type(uint256).max)` first, if the token's ERC-20 allowance to Permit2 is below the amount, then the swap, which carries an empty Permit2 signature and is only directly sendable as-is when a Permit2 allowance to ArcgateRouter already covers the amount, in which case `signatures` is empty too. Otherwise it also returns `signatures: [{ kind: "permit2", typedData }]`; sign `typedData` with the taker's key (EIP-712, e.g. viem's `signTypedData`).
  - **Sign, then call POST /trade/v1/swap/tx** with the same `quoteId`, `taker` and `recipient`, and `permit: { message: typedData.message, signature }`, while the quote is live: free, because this call already paid the swap fee. The first call to it that succeeds uses the round up; a failed one doesn't.
  - Send that response's `transactions` in order.
- **`approval: "approve"` (one call):** returns at most one ERC-20 `approve(ArcgateRouter, amountIn)` transaction instead of a permit to sign - an exact amount, never Permit2, never a signature - and only when the taker's current allowance is below it.
- **Freshness:** the quote lives for the `ttlSec` the quote call asked for (default/max 120s); after that `quoteId` is 410 `quote_expired`. Every call re-quotes and re-simulates at the current block and returns 409 `quote_stale` when the fresh re-quote fails or falls below the stored `minAmountOut`, when the pre-flight simulation reverts on slippage, or when the simulated delivery is below `minAmountOut`. A 409 or 410 carries a free fresh quote in `quote`, with `next: "requote"`: the original quote request (same amount, tokens, side, `slippageBps` and venues, default `ttlSec`) quoted again through the same pipeline, exactly as POST /trade/v1/quote answers it; when the original named a `taker`, the fresh quote is for this call's `taker`, the wallet swapping now. Nothing executes on it: check its price, `safety.verdict` and `readiness`, then swap its `quoteId`. When the fresh quote can't be traded (`no_route`, `insufficient_liquidity`, `unsupported_venue` or `buy_reverts`, a `cannot_sell` or `illiquid` verdict, not executable, or the taker isn't ready) the answer is `next: "stop"` with no `quote`, and `error.hint` says why. One fresh quote per paid quote: a second 409/410 for the same `quoteId`, a quote that itself came from a 409/410, or a quote expired over 5 minutes ago gets plain `requote` with no `quote`, as does one whose re-quote couldn't run or failed on the server's side; then quote again yourself.
- **Fallback:** A stored route on a disabled/undeployed venue falls back to the best executable candidate the quote already priced (warning `route_not_executable`), or 422 `not_executable` when no such candidate exists, none re-quotes, or no ArcgateRouter is configured at all.
- **Attempts:** a quote gets at most 5 failed calls here; the next call on that `quoteId` is 429 `swap_attempts_exhausted` (`next: "requote"`), answered without running the swap pipeline. A failed call is a 409, a 410 (its fresh quote may run), a 422, 500 or 503, or a successful pipeline whose payment settlement or delivery fails. An attempt stays reserved until its 200 is delivered (after settlement when paid); that delivery, a 404, or a 400 (at parse, or a reserved `taker`/`recipient`) uses none. A delivered 200 does not reset this quote's previous failures. POST /trade/v1/swap/tx counts its own, per permit round.
- **Next:** a 200 with `signatures` non-empty needs POST /trade/v1/swap/tx before sending anything (`next: "sign_permit"`); otherwise sign and send `transactions` in order, then confirm the fill with POST /trade/v1/receipt (free).
post.x-price: 0.01 USDC under $1,000; 0.05 USDC from $1,000 to $10,000; above that 0.05 USDC plus 0.5 bps of the amount over $10,000, capped at 5 USDC

tiers.appliesToUsdNotional: < 1,000, a quote with no USD valuation, or unknown/expired quoteId

200.description: Unsigned transactions. When a signature is needed, `signatures[0].typedData` is the Permit2 `PermitSingle` to sign (`next: "sign_permit"`); `transactions` includes the swap with an empty Permit2 signature, not yet embedded - sign, then call POST /trade/v1/swap/tx. When no signature is needed (native-USDC-funded, or an existing Permit2 allowance already covers the amount), `signatures` is empty and `transactions` is directly sendable. `warnings[]` may include `route_not_executable` (fallback route; a truly non-executable route is 422 instead). `approval_fallback` is reserved in the schema for contract stability but is never emitted.

PAYMENT-RESPONSE.description: Settlement receipt for this call's payment (base64 JSON); see the SettleResponse schema for the decoded shape.

post.summary: Sign and send the Permit2 permit a paid POST /trade/v1/swap asked for
post.description:
The free Permit2 second round: finishes a POST /trade/v1/swap call whose `signatures` asked the taker to sign a Permit2 `PermitSingle`.

- **Cost:** free, never x402-gated - a payment header, if one is sent anyway, is ignored and nobody is charged. Only reachable once, right after the paid call that opened it.
- **Key inputs:** the SAME `quoteId`, `taker` and `recipient` (defaults to `taker`) as the paid POST /trade/v1/swap call, plus `deadlineSec` and the required `permit: { message: signatures[0].typedData.message, signature }` (sign `typedData` with the taker's key, EIP-712, e.g. viem's `signTypedData`). `permit` accepts only `message` and `signature`, end to end - any other field, at any level, is 400 `invalid_request` at parse. The service rebuilds the Permit2 domain itself and checks the signer, spender, token, amount, nonce and both deadlines: a mismatched spender or token, or an amount below `amountIn` (a larger amount is accepted), is 400 `invalid_request`; a stale nonce, an expired `sigDeadline`/`expiration`, or an invalid signature (verified via ERC-1271 on chain for a contract taker) is 422 `swap_reverts`. A contract taker can swap, but POST /trade/v1/receipt only reads transactions the taker sends itself, so it answers `invalid_request` for a Safe, ERC-4337 or batching EIP-7702 wallet: check your own transaction receipt instead.
- **No pending round:** 409 `no_pending_swap` when this `quoteId`/`taker`/`recipient` never paid, named a different taker or recipient, or already used its one free call - call POST /trade/v1/swap first, which is paid and returns the permit this call takes.
- **Freshness:** re-quotes and re-simulates exactly like POST /trade/v1/swap, and can answer the SAME 410 `quote_expired`/409 `quote_stale` it would - but never with a fresh `quote` (issue #124's free re-quote is /trade/v1/swap's own paid-quote courtesy, not this free route's).
- **Attempts:** a permit round (`quoteId`, `taker`, `recipient`) gets at most 5 failed calls; the next one is 429 `swap_attempts_exhausted` (`next: "requote"`), answered without running the swap pipeline. A failed call is a 400 from the permit checks above, a 409, 422, 500 or 503, or an undelivered 200; a delivered 200, a 400 at parse, a 404, a 410 or `no_pending_swap` uses none. Failed POST /trade/v1/swap calls don't count here. A new POST /trade/v1/swap permit response resets this round's attempts only once delivered (after settlement when paid).
- **Next:** sign and send `transactions` in order, then confirm the fill with POST /trade/v1/receipt (free). This is the last call in search -> quote -> swap -> swap/tx.

200.description: Unsigned, directly sendable transactions with the permit embedded.

post.summary: Confirm a swap landed: delivered against minAmountOut, pass or fail
post.description:
Tells you whether the transactions POST /trade/v1/swap returned did what the quote promised, once you've sent them. It only reads the chain.

- **Cost:** free, never x402-gated.
- **Key inputs:** `quoteId` (the one you called POST /trade/v1/swap with) and `txHashes`, the 1 to 4 transactions you sent for it: the swap, and any approvals. It answers for a quote /trade/v1/swap handed transactions for in the last hour, else 404 `swap_not_found`, and only for that quote's transactions, sent from its `taker`: an approval to the input token, or a swap to ArcgateRouter whose deadline one of the quote's /trade/v1/swap or /trade/v1/swap/tx answers issued and whose output goes to its `recipient`, else 400 `invalid_request`.
- **Smart-contract wallets:** a Safe, an ERC-4337 account or a batching EIP-7702 wallet sends its transaction from an executor or bundler, or to itself, not from the taker to ArcgateRouter, so this answers 400 `invalid_request` for it. Check that transaction's own receipt and your wallet's success event instead.
- **Returns:** `result`, from the swap transactions. One that filled decides it: `pass` when `delivered` is at least `minAmountOut`, else `fail` (a round 1 that reverted doesn't undo a round 2 that filled). With none filled: `pending` while one is not mined yet, else `fail`: it reverted or was never mined by 60s after its deadline (status `expired`, or `not_found` when the chain never saw it). Approvals are listed but don't change the result. `delivered` is what `recipient` received of `token` (the output), read from the swap transaction's Transfer logs, in base units. Also `block`, each transaction's `status`, and `reason`, one sentence on a fail or pending. The first result from a mined swap is final: asking again returns it.
- **Limits:** one chain read per quote every 5s (the same `txHashes` inside that get the last answer; other hashes get 429 `receipt_rate_limited` with `retryAfterSec`), and at most 132 per quote (then 429 `receipt_reads_exhausted`, for good).
- **Next:** `pass`: tell the user what they bought (`delivered` of `token`). `fail`: follow `next`: `requote` when no swap transaction succeeded (nothing filled; quote again), `stop` when one did (tell them `reason`, and don't trade again). `pending`: ask again in a few seconds.

200.description: What the swap delivered, against the quote's `minAmountOut`.

get.summary: List supported DEX venues and hubs
get.description:
Lists the DEX venues, hub tokens and launchpads this deployment indexes.

- **Cost:** free, never x402-gated.
- **Returns:** each venue with an `executable` flag, hubs and launchpads.
- **Next:** use venue ids in POST /trade/v1/quote's `venues` / `excludeVenues`.

post.summary: Model Context Protocol endpoint (paid tools over x402)
post.description:
The trade API as MCP tools, paid per call with x402.

- **Tools:** every other operation here except `openapi`, named by operationId (tradeSearch, tradeQuote, tradeSwap, tradeSwapTx, tradeReceipt, tradeVenues, health), with the same input schema and the same price.
- **Cost:** tradeSearch, tradeQuote and tradeSwap are paid per call over Arc USDC; tradeSwapTx, tradeReceipt, tradeVenues and health are free. An unpaid `tools/call` returns a tool result with `isError: true` and the payment requirements in `structuredContent`. Sign them and retry with the payment payload in `params._meta["x402/payment"]`; the receipt comes back in `result._meta["x402/payment-response"]`. A result with `isError: true` never settles.
- **Errors:** two error results are @x402/mcp's own and carry no `next`: that payment-required one, and a text-only `Internal Server Error` when the facilitator fails mid-call. Every other error result carries the HTTP route's error body, `next` included, in `structuredContent` and the text content; a call the server refuses (an unknown tool, or arguments the input schema rejects) is `invalid_request`, `next: fix_request`.
- **Client:** use an x402-aware MCP client, e.g. `createx402MCPClient` from `@x402/mcp`.
- **Transport:** Streamable HTTP, stateless, JSON responses. Send `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` or the server answers 406. One JSON-RPC message per request (batches are rejected); bodies up to 16kb.

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description: Must list both media types (MCP Streamable HTTP); anything else gets 406.

200.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 response. Tool errors (including payment required) are results with `isError: true`, not HTTP errors.

202.description: Accepted: a JSON-RPC notification (no response body).

400.description: malformed JSON, not a valid JSON-RPC message, or a JSON-RPC batch (not supported)

406.description: the Accept header must list both application/json and text/event-stream

get.description:
Reports whether the service is up, with its diagnostics.

- **Cost:** free, never x402-gated.
- **Returns:** DB import health, rule set version, the deployed commit, cache/RPC/spend counters and the payer-identity mode.
- **Next:** call before search/quote/swap to check the service is up.

Returns this OpenAPI 3.1 document.

- **Cost:** free, never x402-gated.
- **Returns:** the machine-readable contract for every route, including x402 payment requirements and real examples.

Returns the registration file arcgate's ERC-8004 IdentityRegistry entry points at.

- **Cost:** free, never x402-gated.
- **Returns:** the spec's `type`, `name`, `description`, `image`, `services`, `x402Support`, `active`, `registrations` and `supportedTrust`, plus `arcgate`: the trading network, x402 prices per route, and links to this document, the venues, the docs and the agent skill.
- **Next:** rate arcgate on the ReputationRegistry against the `agentId` in `registrations`.

ttlSec.description: How long the stored quote (and this response's expiresAt) stays live, in seconds (1-120, default 120). A caller may shorten it to re-quote sooner; it can never lengthen past 120s. Safe to shorten or leave at default: POST /trade/v1/swap always re-quotes and re-simulates at the current block and 409s quote_stale below the stored minAmountOut, so this bounds staleness risk, not price risk. The on-chain execution deadline is a separate parameter (deadlineSec, POST /trade/v1/swap).

details.description: Present on 400 invalid_request only: the request's validation issues.

next.description: What to do next. requote: get a new quote, then swap its quoteId. retry: send the same request again, after retryAfterSec when given. fix_request: the request itself is wrong; change it first. stop: don't retry; tell the user. pay: pay the 402 and send the same request again. sign_permit: sign signatures[0].typedData and call POST /trade/v1/swap/tx with `permit`.

retryAfterSec.description: Seconds until the same request can succeed. Only where the server knows it: lookup_rate_limited and receipt_rate_limited.

QuoteReadinessOut.description: Present only when the request names `taker`: can that wallet finish this trade, and what will it cost.

required.description: Raw units of the input token: the amountIn POST /trade/v1/swap spends, for exactOut too (not maxAmountIn). USDC is 6 dp.

available.description: The taker's raw balance of the input token. For USDC, the native balance converted to 6 dp (one balance, native and ERC-20).

approval.description: What POST /trade/v1/swap with the default `approval: "permit2"` needs first. approve: an ERC-20 approve to Permit2. sign_permit: a Permit2 signature (swap returns the typed data). native: the route is paid in native USDC, nothing needed.

approve.description: The same for `approval: "approve"`: an ERC-20 approve to ArcgateRouter, or nothing.

estimatedUsdc.description: best.gasUsdc plus any approve and Permit2 gas the permit2 plan needs, at the quote's base fee.

available.description: The taker's native USDC left for gas: after the trade amount for a USDC input, and after both arcgate fees when the taker pays them in USDC.

enough.description: available covers the gas with POST /trade/v1/swap's 1.3x margin, the check it runs itself; estimatedUsdc is the unmargined cost.

fees.description: The arcgate fee still to pay.

swapUsdc.description: The POST /trade/v1/swap price for this quote; 0 when payment is off. This quote is already paid; POST /trade/v1/swap/tx, which takes the signed permit, is free.

payer.description: The x402 payer of this quote call; null when payment is off or the payer is unknown.

payerAvailable.description: The payer's balance of the fee asset less this quote's own fee, which settles after this answer; null when payer is null or the fee settles on another chain.

enough.description: payerAvailable >= swapUsdc; null when payerAvailable is null (not counted against `ready`).

ready.description: balance.enough and gas.enough, and fees.enough is not false. When false, `next` is `stop`.

next.description: What to do next. requote: get a new quote, then swap its quoteId. retry: send the same request again, after retryAfterSec when given. fix_request: the request itself is wrong; change it first. stop: don't retry; tell the user. pay: pay the 402 and send the same request again. sign_permit: sign signatures[0].typedData and call POST /trade/v1/swap/tx with `permit`.

details.description: On 400 invalid_request: an array of validation issues. On other codes: an object of code-specific context.

next.description: What to do next. requote: get a new quote, then swap its quoteId. retry: send the same request again, after retryAfterSec when given. fix_request: the request itself is wrong; change it first. stop: don't retry; tell the user. pay: pay the 402 and send the same request again. sign_permit: sign signatures[0].typedData and call POST /trade/v1/swap/tx with `permit`.

retryAfterSec.description: Seconds until the same request can succeed. Only where the server knows it: lookup_rate_limited and receipt_rate_limited.

next.description: What to do next. requote: get a new quote, then swap its quoteId. retry: send the same request again, after retryAfterSec when given. fix_request: the request itself is wrong; change it first. stop: don't retry; tell the user. pay: pay the 402 and send the same request again. sign_permit: sign signatures[0].typedData and call POST /trade/v1/swap/tx with `permit`.

details.description: On a 400 invalid_request from body validation: an array of issues ({code, path, message}); other invalid_request cases carry no details. Otherwise, when present, an object of code-specific context, e.g. {requoted, min} / {call, reason} / {delivered, minAmountOut} on quote_stale, or {required, available, token} / {required, available, reason: "gas", swapFee?} on insufficient_balance: those are native 18-decimal amounts, whatever the input (swapFee: this call's own fee, counted when the taker is the x402 payer and pays in USDC on this chain, issue #140). Amounts are base-unit strings, except a USDC input's balance amounts, which are native 18-decimal units.

next.description: What to do next. requote: get a new quote, then swap its quoteId. retry: send the same request again, after retryAfterSec when given. fix_request: the request itself is wrong; change it first. stop: don't retry; tell the user. pay: pay the 402 and send the same request again. sign_permit: sign signatures[0].typedData and call POST /trade/v1/swap/tx with `permit`.

retryAfterSec.description: Seconds until the same request can succeed. Only where the server knows it: lookup_rate_limited and receipt_rate_limited.

quote.description: On 409 quote_stale or 410 quote_expired: a free, fresh quote of the original quote request (same amount, tokens, side, slippageBps and venues; the default ttlSec; when the original named a taker, the wallet calling /trade/v1/swap is the taker), exactly as POST /trade/v1/quote answers it. Nothing executes on it: check its price, safety.verdict and readiness, then swap its quoteId. One per paid quote: absent on a second 409/410 for the same quoteId, for a quote that itself came from here, for a quote expired over 5 minutes, and when the re-quote couldn't run (quote again yourself). Absent with next: stop when the fresh quote can't be traded; error.hint then says why.

purpose.description: "swap" for a transaction to ArcgateRouter, "approve" for one to the input token; null while the chain doesn't know the transaction.

status.description: "expired": a swap transaction the chain knows but never mined, now past its deadline; it can only revert. "not_found": a transaction the chain doesn't know, past the swap's deadline.

delivered.description: What `recipient` received of `token`, from the swap transactions' Transfer logs, in base units. null until every swap transaction is mined.

block.description: The highest block among the swap transactions; null until one is mined.

reason.description: One sentence on a fail or pending result; null on pass.

next.description: Issue #123: retry while pending. After a fail, requote when no swap transaction succeeded, stop when one did (don't trade again); absent on pass.

details.description: On a 400 invalid_request from body validation: an array of issues ({code, path, message}). Otherwise absent.

next.description: What to do next. requote: get a new quote, then swap its quoteId. retry: send the same request again, after retryAfterSec when given. fix_request: the request itself is wrong; change it first. stop: don't retry; tell the user. pay: pay the 402 and send the same request again. sign_permit: sign signatures[0].typedData and call POST /trade/v1/swap/tx with `permit`.

retryAfterSec.description: Seconds until the same request can succeed. Only where the server knows it: lookup_rate_limited and receipt_rate_limited.

PaymentSignature.name: PAYMENT-SIGNATURE
PaymentSignature.description: Sent on the paid retry after a 402: base64 JSON payment payload (PaymentPayload schema), the signed EIP-3009 authorization for the amount in the 402's PAYMENT-REQUIRED header.

x402.name: PAYMENT-SIGNATURE
x402.description: x402 v2 over Arc USDC. Call without this header first: the response is 402 with payment requirements in the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header (base64 JSON, see the PaymentRequired schema). Sign an EIP-3009 authorization for the quoted amount, then retry the SAME request with `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` set to the base64 JSON payment payload (see the PaymentPayload schema). A successful call carries a `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` header with the settlement receipt (see SettleResponse). No 4xx/5xx response ever settles.

PaymentRequired.description: Payment required (x402 v2). Two cases: (1) no or invalid payment - the payment requirements are in the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header. With no payment (or an undecodable one) the body is `{ error: { code: "payment_required", message, hint }, next: "pay" }`, the hint saying to allow Arc USDC in your x402 client and linking the docs; a payment of the wrong amount or one that fails verification gets `{}`; (2) the payment verified and the handler succeeded, but settlement failed - the response carries a PAYMENT-RESPONSE header with `success: false` and an `errorReason`, the handler's result is discarded, the body is `{}`, and nothing was charged. Retry with a fresh payment in either case. The `{}` bodies are written by the x402 middleware itself and carry no `next`.

PAYMENT-REQUIRED.description: Case (1). Base64 JSON payment requirements (PaymentRequired schema): scheme, network, amount, asset, payTo, maxTimeoutSeconds.

PAYMENT-RESPONSE.description: Case (2) only. Base64 JSON settlement result (SettleResponse schema) with `success: false`.

FacilitatorError.description: The x402 facilitator returned an error while verifying or settling payment.

RequestId.description: This call's id in arcgate's logs. Quote it when reporting a problem with the call.
